clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today in terms of scrap or customer complaints, and what decision should real-time data support at the hopper?
clarification_questions.why: Defines whether the goal is root-cause identification, pellet acceptance, or in-line control, which determines whether a sensor is needed at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Goal assumed to be root-cause identification; no sensor is chosen until the contaminant is identified.

clarification_questions.question: Do you know what the black specks consist of (e.g. carbon black, degraded polymer, foreign material), and roughly how often they occur?
clarification_questions.why: The target determines whether any optical method can detect it at all and at what level it matters.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Identity and level unknown; lab screening establishes whether the contaminant is ppm or % level and whether it is spectrally detectable.

clarification_questions.question: Can you provide representative pellet samples, both clean and affected, and describe their colour, form and particle size?
clarification_questions.why: Pellet optical properties and homogeneity decide the probe geometry and whether a specks signal can be seen against the bulk.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pellets assumed opaque solids; optical properties unknown until lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: Which polymer type, grade and additives (including any masterbatch or regrind) are used, and how do they vary between batches?
clarification_questions.why: Polymer and additive identity define the spectral background and whether a calibration or reference can be transferred.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Polymer and additives unknown; any spectral model would be specific to one unidentified matrix.

clarification_questions.question: Do the specks appear only at certain times, after regrind addition, after material changes, or after cleaning or silo changes?
clarification_questions.why: Intermittent or lot-linked occurrence points to a material source rather than a process drift, which changes where measurement is useful.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Occurrence pattern unknown; sampling of incoming lots and hopper material assumed as first step.

clarification_questions.question: Is the hopper accessible for a probe, and how far is it from a location where an analyzer could be placed?
clarification_questions.why: Access and distance decide whether a contact probe, a remote fiber link, or an off-line test is practical.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Hopper access and distance unknown; off-line lab testing of pellet samples assumed before any hopper installation.

clarification_questions.question: What analysis do you currently use to check pellets or parts for contamination, and what accuracy does it give?
clarification_questions.why: A reference method is needed to validate any sensor response and to judge whether a new method adds value.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method exists; lab identification of the specks is the first step.

clarification_questions.question: What response time and detection level would be acceptable, and what is the budget for a trial?
clarification_questions.why: Response time and budget decide whether a simple sensor or a lab-based study is the appropriate first step.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; a lab feasibility study is proposed before any sensor specification.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The claim says AFS shows "NIR reflection" on polymer extrusion. S02 p.14 mentions an NIR probe at the die, but does not state that it is a reflection measurement. The spectra shown are from a diamond ATR probe on an FTIR, not NIR reflection. Fix: Say that AFS shows an NIR probe at the extrusion die and a diamond ATR FTIR probe for API in hot polymer, without specifying NIR reflection.

different_context: The claim applies the NIR diffuse reflection probe and Raman probe to "pellets". S01 p.6 lists the diffuse reflection probe for scattering media and powder, and the Raman probe for liquid, powder and solid. Pellets are not named, and "off-line" for MIR is not stated in any cited page. Fix: Limit the statement to the sample types the table names (powder, scattering media, solid) and remove the unsupported off-line wording, or state that applying these probes to pellets is an assumption to test.

not_supported: S02 p.6 is a transmission-range chart and does not define NIR or Raman coverage categories. It does not say that UV-Vis or Vis-NIR silica fibers give full Raman range coverage, and it does not define the full/partial rule the claim applies. Fix: Report only the transmission ranges shown on the chart, and state that any Raman or NIR full/partial classification is the reviewer's own inference rather than a chart statement.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes, NIR spectrometry and chemometrics. It says nothing about polymer grade, additives, regrind or model validity, and the word "any" overstates the risk. Fix: Remove the claim or cite a page that discusses polymer grade, additive or regrind effects, and soften "can invalidate any model" to "can affect model performance".
